title: Three-month-olds looked longer at a possible event their rule treated as a problem
summary: Luo and Baillargeon report that 3-month-olds looked longer when a tall cylinder showed through a large upper opening in a screen, an event that is physically possible.
body: Yuyan Luo and Renée Baillargeon tested an error of commission: treating a possible event as surprising because a rule is still incomplete. At 3 months, infants looked at a possible event as unexpected, one in which a tall cylinder became visible while passing behind a tall screen that had a very large opening from its top edge. The paper's point is that limited occlusion knowledge can make an ordinary outcome look like a violation. A companion test at about 2.5 months is a separate result and is not this claim. The paper was published in Cognition in 2005. Looking time is the measure, not a verbal judgment.

sources.title: When the ordinary seems unexpected
sources.author: Yuyan Luo and Renée Baillargeon
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Cognition paper, 7 January 2005, PMC3351380. Paraphrase of the 3-month error-of-commission result with the upper opening.
